Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you do a screen-reader audit of the Cedar Clinic appointment page prototype? please keep it to the appointment page and check it with NVDA in Firefox. the parts i need looked at are the date selector, provider dropdown, error message, and confirmation panel. i’m mainly interested in whether the controls and any changes or messages are announced clearly as someone moves through the form and submits it.

this is only a screen-reader audit, so don’t turn it into a general review of the design or a visual contrast or keyboard-only audit. for each issue you find, give the location, what you did, what the screen reader actually announced, and a practical suggested fix. if something can’t be verified from the prototype, please say that rather than guessing. keep the notes concise but specific enough that the page team can locate the issue. send the audit to Leonie, not Emmett. i need the findings, not a rewrite of the page or a claim that anything has already been fixed.", "output": "Conduct a screen-reader audit of the Cedar Clinic appointment page prototype using NVDA in Firefox. Limit the audit to the appointment page and these elements: the date selector, provider dropdown, error message, and confirmation panel. Check whether controls, changes, and messages are announced clearly while a user moves through and submits the form.

Keep this to a screen-reader audit; do not provide a general design review or a visual contrast or keyboard-only audit. For each issue, report its location, what you did, what NVDA actually announced, and a practical suggested fix. If something cannot be verified from the prototype, state that rather than guessing. Keep the findings concise but specific enough for the page team to locate each issue. Send the audit to Leonie, not Emmett. Report findings only; do not rewrite the page or claim that anything has already been fixed."}]
